walkthroughs.body_html:
Rate Equations — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Rate Equations brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Rate Equations.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which species has the same electron configuration as Ar?
options: Na⁺
Cl⁻
F⁻
Mg²⁺

mcqs.q: Successive ionisation energies of an atom always:
options: Decrease
Stay the same
Increase
Vary randomly

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.

Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
Number of protons in the nucleus, which determines the element's identity.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms (or ions): X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.
